title: SPAN: a geometric model of effector tethering in R-loop genome editors
description:
SPAN predicts the activity window of a tethered-effector genome editor from linker statistics, steric exclusion and R-loop geometry. Three parameters are fitted to two published editing profiles and held fixed; all further predictions are made without adjustment. Predictions are scored with each substrate position's deposited coordinate withheld.

The deposit contains the model, the analysis scripts that produce the reported results, and a corpus of 50 published architectures drawn from seven publications, with linker lengths recorded in residues read from construct maps rather than by linker name, and a source register giving the status of every publication examined.

Results: contour length does not move the predicted window across a sixteen-fold range, whereas attachment site does; across 185 buildable terminal-tether designs the predicted peak never falls outside protospacer positions 3 to 12 and reliably falls within 5 to 11, and the span, direction and rigidity a connector would need to reach the remaining positions are given; predicted window position agrees with measurement to within one nucleotide for most SpCas9-family architectures but does not exceed a constant predictor on this corpus; transfer to Cas12a fails by five to six nucleotides, with reach, capture radius, steric map, substrate treatment, fitted parameters and structural substitution eliminated in turn; and the displaced strand's path is not recoverable from linker statistics and steric exclusion, with a median error of 22.8 angstrom in SpCas9 at atomic resolution.
